title: [Phase 4] Implement durable command deduplication and bounded result recovery
criteria: - [ ] Define/implement the canonical authorized command scope and fingerprint from #380: tenant, stable namespace/incarnation and operation, relevant entity and semantically relevant request fields. Preserve payload/media type and define mutable transport budgets versus immutable business inputs explicitly. Same key with a different fingerprint conflicts; no concatenation ambiguity or secret-bearing diagnostic fingerprint dump.

- [ ] Claim a command durably or reserve an unambiguous bounded owner before guest scheduling. Concurrent identical callers observe one owner or explicit in-progress status, with finite coalesced waiter capacity. Duplicate admission must not consume a second guest cell or generate another set of effects.

- [ ] Pin the first accepted command's exact publication/schema and retain that identity for retries/recovery across compatible route or revision changes. Do not include transient revision alone in a namespace that would allow duplicate business execution after rollout. Replaying a historical result rechecks current read authorization and does not renew revoked execution authority.

- [ ] Recover committed results/receipts through #386 without rerunning the guest. Define aborted/never-started/in-progress/interrupted/expired/unknown dispositions and explicit caller retry policy. Do not automatically re-execute interrupted or conflicting commands on restart; not-found after retention expiry is not evidence of nonexecution.

- [ ] Persist and enforce finite deduplication/result retention windows and capacity. Within the promised window, pressure rejects new work rather than silently evicting guaranteed records. Define tombstone/expiry behavior, dedup floors and a bounded status API; distinguish receipt-only from exact full-result replay.

- [ ] Handle cancellation of one duplicate waiter independently of shared work ownership; explicit command/activation cancellation uses the selected identity and commit fence. A rejected/unauthorized duplicate cannot alter the legitimate owner's request, deadline or cancellation state.

- [ ] Tests cover simultaneous identical and conflicting calls, lost response after commit, restart with pending/committed/aborted records, new deployment revision, wrong tenant/principal, namespace recreation, zero/max/oversized keys/results, retention expiry, capacity pressure and dropped duplicate waiters. Count actual guest executions/state commits/effect IDs, not just equal response strings.

- [ ] Include #384's host-derived stable caller/recovery scope in the command identity. Default to the original authenticated caller; shared application/service/integration and delegated scopes are explicit grants. Distinguish stable subject identity from rotating credential bytes. Initial delivery, replay, coalescing and cancellation require their appropriate current application/result permissions, even inside one tenant. Do not bypass a guest-only business permission check by returning cached bytes before authorization.

- [ ] Recover admitted terminal business rejections from #386 as immutable command outcomes during the promised window. A rejected reservation retried after inventory changes still returns its original rejection; deliberate business re-evaluation uses a new command. Rejecting business state/effects does not prohibit durable rejection metadata. Pre-admission auth/validation failure remains a different class.

- [ ] Implement the explicit retry/attempt protocol selected in #380 for a durably proven technical abort after all prior commit owners retire. Guard concurrent retry requests by attempt generation or equivalent linked-command preconditions. Preserve original outcomes and exact fingerprint; no blind identifier replacement, implicit retry, deadline-based abort inference or retry of unknown/expired history. A new attempt cannot be confused with a stale previous completion.

- [ ] Distinguish full result expiry from protective identity retention. Preserve enough linked command/commit identity while unresolved effects, inbox obligations or payload pins require it; #397 owns bounded reclamation. Conservative clock/boot/restore handling must not make a protected command appear new after an unqualified clock jump. Do not promise permanent deduplication after the declared horizon.

- [ ] Add same-tenant different-user/delegation and permission-revocation tests, token rotation for the same subject, lost terminal rejection then changed business state, duplicate explicit retry after confirmed conflict, stale prior-attempt completion, and expired result with a pending/uncertain effect. Count actual guest executions and effects; test replay independently of the original guest's mutation body.

title: [Phase 4] Integrate host-owned transactions with guest execution, commit and cancellation
criteria: - [ ] Instantiate the approved Phase 4 host ABI and sealed transaction context after command admission. Bind every state/intent handle to tenant, namespace, activation, transaction generation, budget and deadline. Pre-admission or incompatible/forged requests must not run a guest or open a write transaction.

- [ ] Implement get/scan/put/delete/intent staging through existing bounded async host machinery. Charge transaction metadata, host/guest copies, staged outputs and in-flight engine work before allocation/submission. Rejected operations remain typed and cannot bypass the shared ledger.

- [ ] Enforce strict policy at preparation and every operation: reject immediate irreversible/unsupported operations and unsupported synchronous service calls. Guest method names or read-only claims are not authority. No automatic guest restart/retry on conflict or failure; existing stateless provider behavior remains unchanged.

- [ ] Support each maintained compiler/engine profile's required runtime imports and suspension behavior under #380/#382's explicit policy. Qualify clocks/entropy/GC/logging and initialization where needed without broadening business-effect grants, introducing a JVM/CLR/Node host, guest OS threads or work surviving activation retirement. Qualified logical runtime work uses #736/the relevant language port, not a language-specific transaction executor. Sharing the core Wasmtime path does not establish per-language compatibility without #389's actual components.

- [ ] Only an eligible successful return with validated/preflighted output submits #386's complete business commit plan. For a composed logical-runtime profile, first settle its required accepted work/continuations under the original transaction authority, budget and deadline, then close staging and sever all guest references before handing owned bytes to commit/recovery. No queued/runnable task can mutate the plan after handoff; no early guest commit or successful commit on unproven quiescence.

- [ ] Declared errors, traps, exhaustion and pre-fence cancellation discard state/intents. Apply the selected language/profile's required error-disposition rules during drain, not a fabricated universal child-error rule. An admitted terminal business rejection uses #386/#387's durable rejection path with no business mutations, rather than being silently retried or mislabelled a successful commit. Idle managed executor workers are not unfinished business tasks; sleeping/daemon work alone is not proof of harmlessness.

- [ ] Implement commit-versus-cancel linearization: cancellation before irreversible commitment aborts; after commitment preserve the committed receipt despite delivery/cleanup failure. During uncertain I/O retain physical owners, budgets and original recovery identity. Dropping a future, promise, task or language waiter is not abort proof.

- [ ] Publish lifecycle/telemetry distinguishing guest completion, transaction disposition, effect delivery and cell cleanup. Preserve finite status/recovery without retaining guest heaps. Durable dispatcher work must not retain a Store/cell/activation once actual guest cleanup finishes.

- [ ] Integrate standalone startup/readiness/drain and authenticated invocation, not only library embeddings. Reject unsupported state/workflow profiles. Bound transactions before execution-cell saturation and preserve the delivered six-language stateless baseline.

- [ ] Validate representative final signatures and imported state/intent values under both direct and HTTP-enabled profiles. Consume #708's preparation regression and #382's checked type/value-limit contract; no global limit inflation or stale prepared/native-cache bypass. Coordinate safe stage/reason projection with #709 without making the entire feedback milestone a prerequisite.

- [ ] Real component tests prove commit, durable rejection, technical abort/conflict, forbidden immediate effects, invalid handles, cancellation before/during/after commit, disconnect, oversized output and successful fresh activation. Pause physical commit work behind barriers to prove no early refund or false abort; cleanup failure preserves durable disposition and quarantines the cell when required.

- [ ] For any newly supported SDK-runtime/transaction composition, prove root return while accepted work is pending, required continuation completion/error before seal, cancellation/deadline during drain, denied late staging after seal, forbidden standard HTTP/stream effects, late wake after Store destruction and fresh cross-tenant reuse. These are that composed profile's enablement tests, not a requirement for core Phase 4 to implement every SDK port.

- [ ] Provide reusable runtime/fixture ports for #389's all-six-language matrix. Each language must execute the core cases through this shared path; language-specific exception/panic, promise/goroutine/task and disposal behavior must be tested by its SDK owner. Do not substitute external-client tests or duplicate the storage/crash campaign six times.

title: [Phase 4] Expose scoped state, command and effect management with CLI recovery workflows
criteria: - [ ] Implement #382's public operation subset: namespace create/inspect/quiesce/retire with generations; command/commit lookup; effect status/history and dispatcher pause/resume; approved reconciliation/redrive/terminal disposition; schema migration; and backup/restore plans/status. Do not expose arbitrary SQL, key editing or raw storage paths as substitutes.

- [ ] Derive actor/tenant from authentication, enforce namespace/publication/provider and data-read authority, and preflight finite request/result/page limits. Known IDs/cursors grant no access. Return exact source/commit/effect/attempt identities without inventing cross-database atomicity. Follow bounded continuation semantics; a short page need not mean completion.

- [ ] Preserve original operation IDs, exact preconditions, historical receipts and ambiguous mutation dispositions. Recover lost responses using their original identity. No hidden polling, mutation replay, ID replacement or refreshing a stale business/management precondition to force success.

- [ ] Reconciliation distinguishes provider-confirmed facts from administrator-declared dispositions. Require a finite current-authorized plan, check retry/deduplication horizon and immutable request identity, and never replay a possibly completed mutation merely because a row is pending. Restored older history follows #399's paused review/resume safeguards.

- [ ] Provide human and lossless JSON output for committed/aborted/conflict/unknown/recovery-required outcomes, rejection replay, expired retention, pending/uncertain/blocked/dead-letter effects and unclean shutdown. Accepted cancel/pause is not proof of physical retirement. Long management operations use bounded shared jobs/status, not a guest workflow engine.

- [ ] Integrate typed audit and bounded-cardinality metrics for transaction conflicts/time/bytes, store pressure, deduplication, active lanes, outbox lag/attempts/policy blocks and physical cleanup. No raw keys/command IDs as unbounded labels or payloads/secrets in diagnostics.

- [ ] A separate real CLI/node test configures a namespace, commits, loses/recovers the response, inspects effect/history, pauses/resumes, exercises compatible migration/backup/restore review and rejects wrong tenant, stale plans and unsafe redrive. Cover output limits, audit failure, disconnect and exact original-operation recovery.

- [ ] Deliver the first supported namespace -> command -> lost response -> original-result recovery -> effect-inspection slice when #382/#384/#387/#388 and relevant #391 ports exist. Do not wait to begin until every migration/backup command is complete or introduce a temporary second protocol. Final closure still requires the full management scope.

- [ ] Enforce #384/#387 current result-read/application authorization and stable caller/delegated scope for initial delivery, replay and cancellation. Cover same-tenant users, withdrawn delegation, token rotation and postcommit access revocation; execution permission and knowledge of an ID are insufficient.

- [ ] Expose durable terminal business rejection separately from successful business commit and proven technical abort. Only #380/#387's explicit fenced retry is available after affirmative no-commit/retired-owner proof. Preserve original fingerprints, user expected versions and prior attempt/result history; unknown/expired status is not retry authorization.

- [ ] Expose finite retained-format and pending/uncertain-work inventories, linked retention holds and time-continuity problems. Do not rewrite old intents, transfer authority to a new publication, renew revoked grants or delete protective records to clear an error.

- [ ] Wire #397's reserved recovery admission into actual authenticated status/pause/reconciliation, engine jobs, durable disposition writes and responses. With ordinary queues full and storage at its configured high-water mark, prove finite supported recovery progress. Unreadable/stuck storage can fail explicitly, never claim unlimited recovery or refund a live owner's permit.

- [ ] Extend the real CLI/node tests with lost rejection followed by changed business state, concurrent explicit retries after confirmed abort, saturated ordinary queues plus recovery inspection/pause and pending old-format work at retirement. Retain actual execution/effect counts and physical-owner evidence.

- [ ] Integrate safe producer-defined preparation/admission/runtime/commit/provider reasons through the existing public error boundary, coordinating #709's authorized correlation. Distinguish failure stage from durable disposition. Do not expose arbitrary engine text, secret paths, credentials or guest payloads to public/browser callers. Missing diagnostics are not proof of nonexecution.

- [ ] Supply non-mutating namespace/profile/target inspection useful to #710 composition preflight and #716 target resolution. Return coherent observed generations and currentness caveats; inspection creates no grant/reservation, executes no mutating guest and cannot replace acceptance-time checks. Reuse original route/publication resolution rather than requiring a denied invocation as a probe.

- [ ] Let existing #563/#564/#565 build/watch/test controllers and #633/#641 publication/route workflows consume the same APIs. A developer edit or restart must preserve state/command identity and last-good deployment without forced generation refresh, hidden business-command retries or automatic purge. Keep controller-owned workflow journals distinct from durable command records.

- [ ] Reuse existing protected local/SSH/WSL/private-container management paths where supported; no public RPC bind, browser management token or new privileged gateway. Toolkit transport identity, operator permission and guest capability authority remain distinct.

title: [Phase 4 Gate] Validate atomic business state, durable effects, recovery and bounded resource ownership
criteria: - [ ] #380 — Host-owned transaction, isolation and durable outcome contract.
- [ ] #381 — Selected embedded-engine qualification and durability profile.
- [ ] #382 — Versioned WIT/RPC/host contracts with separate guest/client profiles.
- [ ] #383 — Bounded local store owner and restart-safe format.
- [ ] #384 — Namespace identity, sealed authority and lifecycle fences.
- [ ] #385 — Bounded OCC with phantom-safe prefix reads.
- [ ] #386 — Atomic state/outbox/command-result/inbox persistence.
- [ ] #387 — Durable command deduplication and result recovery.
- [ ] #388 — Shared guest/activation/commit/cancellation integration.
- [ ] #389 — All six guest SDKs: transactions, read-only queries, intents, templates and real component tests.
- [ ] #718 — Required Java guest implementation, HTTP integration and recovery slice contributing to #389.
- [ ] #390 — Durable effect authority and lifetime.
- [ ] #391 — Bounded dispatcher, claims, retry and uncertainty states.
- [ ] #392 — Real JetStream effect delivery.
- [ ] #393 — Qualified idempotent HTTP/reconciliation profile.
- [ ] #394 — Ephemeral entity ownership lanes.
- [ ] #395 — Transactional inbox and post-commit acknowledgement.
- [ ] #396 — Durable immutable payload retention.
- [ ] #397 — Quotas, linked retention, GC and compaction.
- [ ] #398 — State/retained-format rollout, migration and rollback compatibility.
- [ ] #399 — Consistent backup and guarded restore.
- [ ] #400 — Authenticated management/CLI/audit and recovery.
- [ ] #401 — All six external clients extended and independently tested.
- [ ] #402 — Shared stateful application and real browser recovery workflow.
- [ ] #403 — Integrated adversarial/crash/conformance matrix with guest/client evidence separated.
- [ ] #404 — Fixed/active/shared resource and latency evidence, including each guest profile.
- [ ] #405 — Native and developer bundles, clean-host workflows, compatible upgrades and retained state.
- [ ] #406 — Versioned practical guest/client/operations guides and actual Pages publication.
- [ ] #408 — Read-only queries, fresh views and stale-edit preconditions without durable query command rows.
- [ ] #409 — Shared-HTTP transactional commands, queries and authorized result recovery.

- [ ] Every scoped implementation is merged and its exact source/test identities map to requirements. Resolve correctness, authority, data-loss and physical-cleanup blockers instead of closing from models or unrelated historical runs.

- [ ] Real guest commands atomically persist state, intents, command result/deduplication and applicable inbox records under the declared isolation model. No early guest commit, phantom anomaly, stale-authority commit or implicitly repeated immediate mutation. Current stateless behavior remains supported.

- [ ] Controlled failures/crashes before/during/after commit, acknowledgement and response delivery preserve committed/aborted/unknown distinctions. Recover original results without duplicate state/effects; retention and expiry are explicit.

- [ ] Real provider evidence distinguishes accepted delivery, known failure, uncertain mutation, safe bounded retries and blocked/expired/dead-letter reconciliation. Credential/provider changes do not widen committed work; no universal exactly-once claim.

- [ ] Entity queues, engine jobs/read views, blobs, claims, buffers and maintenance are finite and retire exactly once or remain truthfully owned/quarantined. Dormant entities and pending outbox records own no guest Store/cell/process/thread/listener/timer or language heap. Independent work progresses under the declared hot-key/outage load.

- [ ] Actual migration, compatible/incompatible canary/rollback, backup integrity, disk pressure/corruption and older-history restore pass. Restored pending work for a remotely completed effect does not replay automatically. Current revocation authority is not overwritten with historical grants.

- [ ] **All six guest entries pass:** actual authored Rust, C, TypeScript, Go, Java and C#/.NET components compile through their maintained recipes, package/sign/admit and execute transaction, query and staged-intent cases on a real Linux node. Cover business rejection, conflict/stale edits, lost response/recovery, denial, memory/fuel limits, cancellation and fresh-state cleanup, including language-specific ownership/exception/async/runtime-import behavior. External-client tests, host-native unit tests, generated stubs, unsupported skips or two-language examples cannot satisfy a missing guest entry.

- [ ] **All six external-client entries pass separately:** existing transports execute the common #401 profile and language-specific cancellation, ownership, malformed-response and shutdown cases against a separate node. Shared vectors and a reviewed pairing plan avoid requiring 36 client×guest combinations; every required surface and language still has real evidence.

- [ ] Authenticated native and developer distributions complete #405's clean-host setup, create/build/test and retained restart/upgrade/removal/purge workflows on supported platforms. Reuse Windows/WSL2 and Linux/direct/SSH/devcontainer tooling without claiming a Windows production node, Mac/ARM64 support or Linux durability from the narrower portable host. Native server operation needs no guest compiler, external database or mandatory container runtime.

- [ ] The maintained application works through actual shared HTTP ingress and a browser, retaining read-only SSR/hydration, protected mutations, safe state-dependent caching and original-result recovery. #402 reuses one UI/scenario set with six guest backends for its core flow, not six independent apps. Java #718 supplies real transactional HTTP evidence; synthetic browser fulfilment and isolated provider success are insufficient.

- [ ] Review #404's declared measurements for physical process/thread/cell/heap/I/O/durable bytes, plateaus, useful latency/throughput, per-guest active/runtime costs, restart and maintenance. Preserve failures/unavailable values and distinguish configured limits, process-crash evidence and power-loss assumptions. No universal fixed RSS, cross-language speed ranking or production SLO.

- [ ] Publish/walk through #406's version-matched guides for all six guests and six external clients with source-backed language switching, supported profile limits and recovery. Candidate/docs review may precede a final release tag. Current Docusaurus mechanisms are reused; retired Wiki publication and obsolete alpha shims are not gate requirements.

- [ ] Publish one compact completion decision and machine-checkable requirement/evidence map. Identify component/tool/runtime/profile/source and actual executed scope for each guest and client entry; update support/roadmap only after review. Keep previous phase/evidence bytes unchanged.

- [ ] #408 proves coherent bounded read snapshots, no business writes/intents or mandatory query command/result rows, fresh read after acknowledged commit and explicit stale-screen preconditions. Ordinary restart preserves acknowledged state; older-history restore changes view/recovery identity.

- [ ] #409 provides reusable HTTP command/query/recovery behavior, not app-only logic. Real sockets/browser tests cover lost response after commit, precommit response validation, no GET/SSR mutations, safe caches, no replayed historical security cookies and finite cleanup. Actual preparation on the final profile includes the #708 regression where applicable; safe diagnostics/preflight distinguish validation from execution rather than hiding failures.

- [ ] #384/#387/#400/#401/#409 prove current result-read/application permission during initial delivery/replay, including same-tenant users, entity access, withdrawn delegation, token rotation and postcommit revocation. Known IDs and historical execution grants provide no bypass.

- [ ] #386/#387/#395 prove durable terminal-rejection recovery with zero business writes/effects, despite lost responses/acks and later state changes. Explicit technical-abort retry has no-commit and retired-owner proof plus a concurrency fence. Unknown/expired outcomes are not retry permission.

- [ ] #390/#391/#395/#398/#405 preserve or refuse required retained intent/result/rejection/inbox/ordering/checkpoint formats across updates. Pending work at ordinary retirement is inspectable; emergency revocation denies further unauthorized dispatch. No silent decoder removal, history deletion or authority transfer.

- [ ] #387/#395/#396/#397/#399 prove linked identity/payload retention after result-body expiry and conservative clocks/reboot/restore. Finite quotas and explicit reconciliation bound unresolved work without erasing protective records.

- [ ] #397/#400 prove physically usable finite authenticated status/pause/reconciliation while ordinary queues/storage are at declared limits. A genuinely unreadable/stuck device can fail explicitly, never refund live permits or fabricate recovery.

- [ ] #403 maps each boundary to actual focused/integrated evidence; #404 quantifies costs; #389/#718/#401/#402/#405/#406 supply six-guest, six-client, application, distribution and guide evidence. Shared lower-level storage/provider tests may be reused only under their exact source/scope; reuse cannot replace a language's own execution proof.

title: [Phase 4] Implement bounded read-only state queries without durable command writes
criteria: - [ ] Define the approved query mode through #380/#382: one authenticated tenant and authorized namespace, one bounded consistent read view, point reads and supported paged prefix reads, explicit view/schema/namespace-incarnation identity, and no business-state mutations or staged effects. Reuse the selected engine, generated host bindings, resolver, admission, scheduler and fresh Wasmtime activation path; do not create another query executor or database.

- [ ] Enforce read-only authority at preparation and every host operation, not only through an SDK helper or caller flag. Deny put/delete, intent staging, early commit and unsupported mutating/child/provider paths even for a malicious guest. Permitted runtime-support imports, logging and audit follow #380/#382's explicit classification; a necessary clock/entropy/GC import is neither broad effect authority nor a reason to exclude a supported guest language.

- [ ] Do not allocate durable business command deduplication, replay-result, inbox or outbox rows, advance application state versions or reserve write quota merely because a read succeeds. Normal bounded activation status, telemetry and required security/audit records remain allowed; do not advertise zero physical I/O or disable audit to meet this criterion.

- [ ] Define a fresh-view acquisition point after query acceptance. Without an explicitly supported historical-view request, a query started after a command's commit acknowledgement reads a snapshot no older than that commit on the same node/namespace incarnation, including acknowledged commits recovered after ordinary restart. Concurrent later writes follow the captured snapshot. Never present an older cache/view as current; older-history restore establishes a different recovery epoch and cannot satisfy an incompatible minimum-version expectation.

- [ ] Keep query reads consistent across supported pages. Bind cursors to the original authorized scope, view and query, with finite lifetime/bytes/pages and current access checks. A cursor cannot silently open a newer snapshot after eviction, expiry or restart. Cross-invocation historical snapshot retention is not required; unsupported continuation fails explicitly rather than retaining a guest/entity. Clients must follow continuation tokens even when a byte bound produces fewer items than requested.

- [ ] Bound active views, snapshot age, keys, page/aggregate bytes, buffers, pending engine jobs and cancellation cleanup. Do not retain an exclusive writer lock across guest execution. Dropped waiters retain physical I/O/read owners until retirement; repeated views cannot indefinitely block maintenance. Snapshot reads do not require entity serialization or consume all execution cells merely waiting on a hot key.

- [ ] Expose typed query results and view tokens through the authoritative host/RPC profile, preserving exact unsigned/presence/byte semantics and current authorization. Include the maintained example of loading a version and supplying that original expected version in a later command: activation OCC does not detect that a user edited an older screen. The precondition participates in the command fingerprint and is never refreshed automatically after uncertainty.

- [ ] Engine-backed real-component tests cover concurrent multi-key updates without mixed snapshots, acknowledged-commit-then-query freshness, no durable command/outbox growth from repeated reads, attempted query writes/effects, wrong tenant and same-tenant denied principal, stale cursor, namespace recreation, schema change, expiry/cancellation with paused physical I/O and a successful fresh query after failure. Assert actual rows, versions and owner retirement, not only method names or mocked values.

- [ ] Provide shared fixtures and generated contract vectors for all six guest integrations in #389/#718 and all six client integrations in #401. Verify language-specific binding ownership, async suspension, errors and full-width values through their actual components/transports. Reuse the same query engine and small scenario set; no six alternative query implementations or mandatory 36-way client×guest matrix.

- [ ] Validate query signatures and values under the intended direct and HTTP-enabled engine profiles, including safe/over-limit nested/list values and preparation-cache identity. Reuse the #708 regression where relevant. Query/read-only success cannot bypass value-lifting bounds, signed admission or runtime authorization merely because no business write occurs.

title: [Phase 4] Integrate transactional commands, queries and result recovery with shared HTTP ingress
criteria: - [ ] Define a versioned application-route binding for command, query and result recovery. Pin approved application/operation/contract, tenant, namespace/incarnation, selected publication and any entity mapping before execution. Enforce route/current-authority fences through admission and commitment; request headers cannot select arbitrary namespaces, functions or management authority.

- [ ] Map a bounded application command ID and canonical request fingerprint to #387 before guest scheduling. Derive caller/recovery scope from authenticated context with explicit policy for shared/delegated scope. Decide which path/query/body/media-type/precondition fields are business input; rotating credentials, CSRF tokens and transport deadlines are not business identity. Reject ambiguous encodings, duplicate IDs and changed operation/entity/body rather than silently colliding them.

- [ ] Expose authenticated purpose-specific result lookup without management bearer credentials, provider secrets or arbitrary database access. Recheck current result-read/application authorization on initial delivery and replay; do not bypass guest-only business checks by returning cached results. Users in one tenant cannot read, cancel or coalesce another user's command merely by knowing its ID. Explicit delegation is policy-bound and tested.

- [ ] Reuse #388's single commit owner. Validate bounded response structure, headers/cookies/media/body and promised replay data before business commitment wherever the host controls validation. Do not send success before the promised durable disposition. Disconnect/write failure after commitment preserves original committed history, not an aborted classification or automatic re-execution.

- [ ] Define replay precisely: retained approved application result or an explicit receipt-only envelope, with current transport/security policy reapplied. Never reissue old session/CSRF credentials, one-time tokens or historical Set-Cookie as newly authorized data. Unrepresentable required replay forms reject before commitment; a retained digest or receipt cannot be advertised as full-response replay.

- [ ] Route ordinary reads/SSR through #408 without mandatory durable command/result rows. GET/HEAD and render navigation cannot mutate merely because a command key is present. Implement fresh read-after-ack and explicit stale-edit expected versions; never replace a caller's original precondition on conflict or uncertainty. Keep renderer read authority narrow and distinct from the command's write authority.

- [ ] Preserve the **actually supported** host-owned origin/Fetch Metadata/CORS/CSRF/cookie/CSP, proxy, asset and response-cache policies. New cross-origin static-asset grants do not authorize application API access. Personalized/state-dependent query and command responses default to no-store/non-shared. No historical response or route change may widen cache/auth scope. An opt-in mutable-state cache is not required and needs separate correctness proof.

- [ ] Define bounded HTTP mappings for success, durable business rejection, proven-aborted conflict, in-progress, committed-with-lost-delivery, unknown/retention-expired and forbidden recovery. HTTP status and durable disposition remain separate; Retry-After, 5xx or a lost connection is not resubmission authority. Status requests are finite explicit operations, not a persistent application poller.

- [ ] Retain request/result buffers, cancellation registrations, storage/network owners and effect references until actual retirement. Query/command ingress shares normal finite admission and drain. Result retrieval never reruns the original mutating guest; any approved read-only authorization evaluation follows #384/#408's bounds. Pending external delivery holds no guest cell after guest cleanup. Preserve physically usable administrative recovery capacity under #397/#400.

- [ ] Real node/socket/browser tests cover submission and authorized lookup, lost response after commit, same-key changed input/entity/operation, token rotation/login change, same-tenant denial and revoked replay access, rejection after business data changes, explicit retry only after proven abort, stale edits, query freshness, mutation-via-GET denial, invalid/oversized response before commit, cookie/token protection, cache isolation and disconnect during physical cleanup. Count actual guest executions/commits/effects; browser fulfilment mocks are not proof.

- [ ] Freeze usable mappings with #382/#389 for all six maintained guest profiles, including normal typed result/error and ownership semantics. Supporting a language does not require it to implement a new HTTP listener or import an external client. Early runtime fixtures may use one language; #389/#718/#402/#403 supply final real-component coverage for every required language.

- [ ] Define the transaction root explicitly. An existing stateless HTTP adapter's synchronous local-service hop does not create a cross-service transaction, delegate end-user authority automatically or override strict child-call restrictions. Use a host-approved direct command/query binding or another explicitly specified supported composition; reject unsupported nesting without running immediate effects.

- [ ] Qualify the final Java command/query/HTTP path using #718's actual signed component and the minimized #708 signature-preparation regression where applicable. Check exact WIT surface and finite value-lifting plans under the selected HTTP engine profile, not only schema, standalone invocation or isolated outbound-HTTP success. Profile changes invalidate incompatible preparation/native-cache identities; do not solve a failure by indiscriminately inflating limits or erasing types.

- [ ] Reuse #709/#710's safe diagnostics/composition checks and #713/#716's response/target helpers as those interfaces become available. Distinguish structural checks, actual preparation, current authorized state and executed requests. A preflight is not a grant and must not execute a mutating command; normal acceptance always rechecks authority. Necessary local validation must not depend on the entire feedback milestone closing.

- [ ] Compose with existing static and renderer routes without another router. Preserve API precedence, missing-resource behavior, host-owned headers, independent publication identities and explicit rollback/recovery. Current static-site/TypeScript API examples (#632) are a baseline, not evidence that transactional Java or the other guest profiles already work.
